interpretation: Short source-grounded summaries are separated from editorial application guidance. All examples/counterexamples are synthetic; no real campaign histories, outcomes or personal agency experience are claimed. Principles are contextual tools, not universal templates.

sources.title: Runco and Jaeger (2012), The Standard Definition of Creativity
sources.limitations: Original journal article hosted by DISF; definition/review, not effectiveness evidence for these concepts.

sources.title: Gentner (1983), Structure-Mapping: A Theoretical Framework for Analogy
sources.limitations: Original article hosted by author laboratory. Theory of analogy is not evidence that a particular visual metaphor will be understood.

sources.title: Green and Brock (2000), The role of transportation in the persuasiveness of public narratives
sources.limitations: Author university record and abstract reviewed; full article not reviewed here. Narrative-reading experiments do not establish effects of a single static image.

sources.title: Daniel Simons Visual Cognition Lab research
sources.limitations: Researcher laboratory summary, not a complete study report; attention experiments do not provide ad-response rates or a universal attention span.

sources.title: Ehrenberg-Bass Distinctive Asset Measurement
sources.limitations: Institute service summary; actual recognition, attribution and asset strength require measurement.

sources.title: Stanford d.school Design Project Scoping Guide
sources.limitations: Framework-owner practice guide; iteration is not proof of quality, independent evidence or validated campaign impact.

principles.title: Strategic creativity serves the assigned takeaway
principles.sourceSummary: Creativity combines originality with effectiveness or appropriateness; novelty alone is insufficient.
principles.application: Evaluate ideas against the same proposition and audience takeaway. Express the selected strategy rather than inventing a different brand promise.
principles.limits: Effectiveness here means assignment fit, not measured sales. No concept has qualified validation.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: express an everyday bottle through departure preparation while preserving the capacity fact.
principles.counterexample: An unusual performance promise is not appropriate simply because it is novel.

principles.title: A concept is a communicative relationship, not surface styling
principles.sourceSummary: Originality needs a context in which usefulness or appropriateness is judged.
principles.application: Describe what makes the idea work in one sentence. Separate the conceptual premise from final copy and layout. Develop two routes with materially different premises.
principles.limits: Literal duplicate detection cannot prove subjective originality or distinctness. There is no requirement for a universal idea template.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: a departure ritual and a symbolic place in the daily routine are different premises for one proposition.
principles.counterexample: Changing a background color while keeping the same scene is not necessarily another concept.

principles.title: Map the relevant relationship and inspect unintended claims
principles.sourceSummary: Analogy can transfer relational structure between domains rather than merely matching surface attributes.
principles.application: For a metaphor, identify the intended mapping, likely interpretation and where it breaks. Keep metaphorical meaning separate from literal product proof.
principles.limits: A plausible mapping is not evidence that the audience will understand it. Avoid metaphors that imply unsupported capabilities.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: a bottle represented as a punctuation mark in a day suggests a routine pause; no medical effect is implied.
principles.counterexample: Showing a bottle as a battery must not imply proven energy or performance effects.

principles.title: Use a relevant situation or story only when it clarifies
principles.sourceSummary: The reviewed abstract examines absorption into narratives and story-consistent beliefs and evaluations.
principles.application: A static can suggest a situation and an intended takeaway without a full plot. Use the brief’s context; test whether the audience interprets the intended relationship.
principles.limits: Applying narrative findings to one static is an editorial hypothesis. Do not invent testimonials or real campaign histories.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: departure preparation suggests when the bottle might enter a routine.
principles.counterexample: Do not label an invented customer success story as an authentic testimonial.

principles.title: Attention is selective; salience is not understanding
principles.sourceSummary: People can miss visible events outside the focus of attention in laboratory tasks.
principles.application: Identify what must be noticed and understood. Challenge competing elements and unintended readings; let specialists resolve actual copy and visual hierarchy.
principles.limits: No fixed attention span, recall rate or conversion effect follows from this summary. Feasibility depends on the supplied format and final execution.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: check whether a playful metaphor still lets viewers identify the actual product.
principles.counterexample: A surprising object alone does not prove the proposition was understood or remembered.

principles.title: Preserve brand connection while exploring a premise
principles.sourceSummary: Brand-linked assets can support recognition; the institute advocates measuring their linkage and protecting them over time.
principles.application: Continuity uses supplied approved language and cues. Exploration varies the premise while preserving explicit requirements, established positioning and recognizability.
principles.limits: Observed repeated styling is not measured asset strength. No branding cue can be removed merely because exploration is desired.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: retain a supplied brand mark and product identity in a new symbolic situation.
principles.counterexample: Do not call a fictional new color a famous brand asset or confuse exploration with rebranding.

principles.title: Make critique specific and bounded
principles.sourceSummary: The guide treats project context, iteration and low-resolution prototypes as tools for advancing design work.
principles.application: Challenge clarity, relevance, truth, brand connection, distinction and feasibility. Record specific risks and refinements. Mandatory failures block the pair rather than selecting a favorite.
principles.limits: Repeated model passes are not independent evidence. Two bounded attempts represent workflow limits, not executed retries or validated improvement.
principles.syntheticExample: Synthetic: refine a metaphor after noticing it could imply an unsupported health benefit.
principles.counterexample: A high qualitative preference score cannot compensate for a false claim or mandatory-rule violation.
